data.long_meaning: Derived from 'azaba' which means 'to threaten' or 'to attack'. This name is mentioned in the Quran as a name of a powerful enemy army that was confronted by Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The name Ahzab carries the meaning “Group or Army” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ahzab usually hope their child will grow to embody group or army and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Ahzab
in_english.meaning: Groups, parties, or factions, especially those opposed to Muslims
in_english.long_meaning: Ahzab is an Arabic term used in Islamic history and the Quran to describe coalitions or groups that united against the Muslim community in Medina. The term is derived from the Arabic root 'ḥ-z-b' which means 'to gather' or 'to collect'. The most notable reference to Ahzab is in Surahs Al-Imran and Al-Ahzab, which recount the Battle of the Trench, where various tribes and groups formed an alliance to besiege and attack the Muslims in Medina. The term holds significant historical and spiritual meaning in Islamic tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ahzab' is significant in Islamic history as it represents a time when the early Muslim community was faced with a formidable enemy threat. The Battle of the Confederates, also known as the Battle of the Trench, was a major military conflict that took place in Medina, Saudi Arabia, in the year 627 CE. This battle saw the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions successfully defend their territory against an enemy coalition that was four times larger in number. The victory at this battle is often considered a turning point in the early Islamic history and demonstrated the resilience and determination of the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Ahzab' serves as a reminder of the trials and challenges that believers may face in their lives. In the Quran, it is stated that every hardship experienced by a person contains a relief, and this is often referred to as a 'cure' for the soul. Therefore, the name Ahzab, coming from a time of major spiritual and physical test for the early Muslim community, serves as a reminder that all difficulties and challenges can ultimately be overcome with courage, determination, and faith in God. This spiritual significance resonates with all Muslims throughout history and continues to inspire them in times of personal and collective struggles.
